instruction_summary: Recalibrate Blanchard & Katz (1992)'s migration-adjustment model on state data through 2025: re-estimate its central migration elasticity, make the minimal amendment (a declining migration-responsiveness parameter) that reconciles the 1992 and 2026 evidence, validate out-of-sample and on the Great-Recession/COVID windows, and quantify what slower adjustment implies for the duration of local slumps.

steps.description: Read replication artifacts, 001 report/summary/CSVs, and re-read the paper's model section (eq. 4-7, pp. 15-22; closed form p. 18)
Rebuilt the venv (pandas 3.0.5, numpy 2.5.2, statsmodels 0.14.6 per evidence_summary) and installed pymupdf
steps.command: uv venv /workspace/.venv && uv pip install numpy pandas scipy statsmodels matplotlib pyarrow pymupdf

steps.description: Directly estimated BK's migration equation (rel. labor-force & population growth on lagged rel. unemployment, +/- income; state FE, state-clustered SE) per era and in rolling windows -- reusing 001's panel

Calibrated the two-margin adjustment model (m,a) from 001's estimated moments (VAR migration share, UR half-life) per era; built paper-vs-2026 calibration table; ran slump-duration counterfactual; held-out (pre-2015 vs 2015-24) and COVID-episode validation

Built the 4-panel original-vs-updated figure (migration responsiveness, adjustment composition, model fit + counterfactual, slump duration over time), reusing the replication's AR->IRF engine for the empirical UR IRFs
Wrote the theory section, report, and cards

key_results.UR_halflife_GFC_window_1995_2009: 5.0 yr; time-to-80%-recovery 11.6 yr; cum10 UR 1.56 vs 0.33 paper-era [ESTIMATED/CALIBRATED]
key_results.counterfactual_price_of_immobility: restoring paper-era migration cuts one-off half-life 3.0->2.7 yr and cumulative slump -10% [CALIBRATED]
key_results.held_out_elasticity_pre2015_vs_2015_2024: 0.00370 -> 0.00076 (5x lower out of sample); pre-2015 m over-predicts out-migration [ESTIMATED]
key_results.COVID_episode: emp_lr -0.22 (V-shaped); updated model (m=0.043,a=0.163) reproduces small non-permanent loss -0.21; original high-migration model cannot [CALIBRATED]
key_results.amendment: declining time-varying migration-responsiveness parameter g_t = footprint of rising real moving costs (housing); alternative explicit HPI moving-cost margin considered and rejected [PROPOSED]

comparison_to_original.quantity: structural migration elasticity m = -d(rel labor force)/d(rel unemployment)
comparison_to_original.original: not estimated by the paper or 001
comparison_to_original.note: new direct structural estimate of BK eq.7; ~halved, ~7-sigma paper-era

comparison_to_original.quantity: UR-gap half-life / duration of a local slump (one-off shock)
comparison_to_original.note: one-off unchanged (composition rotates m->a); genuine lengthening only for severe persistent shocks
permanence weakened as migration share fell (-m/S)

deviations: The two-margin (m,a) adjustment model is a stylized single-mode reduction of BK's richer dynamics, exactly-identified from two moments; it is a calibration device for the slump-duration counterfactual, labelled [CALIBRATED]. The directly estimated migration elasticity is the genuine [ESTIMATED] structural quantity.

One-off UR half-life did NOT lengthen (honest tension with the instruction's premise): it resolves as a composition rotation (migration m down, job-recovery a up), with genuine lengthening confined to the severe/persistent GFC window (H 3->5). Reported as found.

Housing/cost-of-moving margin is modelled as the reduced-form declining parameter g_t, not estimated from a state house-price panel (out of reuse scope; 001 did not build HPI). The explicit-HPI alternative was considered and rejected for identification/parsimony.

Data scope unchanged from 001/replication: LAUS state coverage from 1976; relative per-capita income as BK's Fig-13 wage proxy (composition-adjusted CPS wages and SIC manufacturing AHE unreconstructable). No new data downloaded; compute was estimation + calibration only, per the brief.
